findings.title: line_total quantizes unit price to cents before multiplying, double-rounding the total
findings.evidence: parse_money(unit_price) is called first, so a unit price of 0.005 becomes 0.01 before the multiply; line_total('0.005', 1000) returns 10.00 instead of 5.00.
findings.recommendation: Convert unit_price without quantizing (e.g. Decimal(str(unit_price)) after the float/type guard) and apply the single ROUND_HALF_UP quantize only to the final product; if per-unit prices are contractually cent-precise, validate that explicitly and raise instead of silently rounding.

findings.title: Only float is rejected; None/bool/NaN inputs escape as decimal.InvalidOperation or NaN
findings.evidence: The guard rejects float only, then fallback Decimal(str(value)) raises an opaque InvalidOperation for None/True and lets Decimal('NaN') flow through, so callers cannot catch a single documented error type.
findings.evidence_quote: amount = value if isinstance(value, Decimal) else Decimal(str(value))
findings.recommendation: Validate the accepted types explicitly (str/int/Decimal) and raise TypeError otherwise; also reject non-finite Decimals with amount.is_finite() before quantizing, and wrap conversion failures in a clear exception.

findings.title: tax_rate bypasses the float guard and accepts negative rates
findings.evidence: tax_rate is converted via Decimal(str(tax_rate)), so floats are silently accepted here even though parse_money rejects them; a negative or nonsensical rate produces a negative tax with no error.
findings.recommendation: Route tax_rate through the same validation helper as monetary values (reject float or document float support) and range-check the rate (e.g. 0 <= rate <= 1) before computing.

findings.title: No tests accompany the new money helpers
findings.evidence: The diff adds the module only; the change context states no test commands were run, so rounding order, negative quantity, and float-rejection behaviour are unverified.
findings.recommendation: Add unit tests covering: sub-cent unit prices with large quantities, float input rejection, negative quantity, None/bool input, non-finite Decimals, and tax rounding at the half-cent boundary.
